items.title: Apec summit live: Xi and Putin start talks; Rubio says Trump serious about meeting Kim Jong-un
items.summary:
Summit in Chinese tech hub Shenzhen set to include highly anticipated meeting between Xi, Trump and Putin

  • Shenzhen takes centre stage as Xi sends ‘Chinamaxxing’ message at Apec summit

  • What is Apec? Explained in 30 seconds

The Australian prime minister, Anthony Albanese, has arrived in Shenzhen for the Apec summit, and confirmed he will join a leaders’ “family photo” despite the presence of Russia’s Vladimir Putin.

Albanese said he would respect the wishes of host country China and take part, echoing the explanation of the Canadian prime minister, Mark Carney. But, Albanese said would make clear Australia’s view on Russia’s invasion of Ukraine.

This is a big power intervening in an illegal way to try to assert its will and underestimating the will and courage and conviction of the Ukrainian people to fight for their national sovereignty.

Absolutely there is a role for middle power diplomacy, and we’ll see at Apec, the engagement that we’ll have with countries such as Canada and Mexico, Korea, Japan.

They are important partners for Australia.

Continue reading...
items.t: Apec summit live: Xi and Putin give opening speeches as world leaders gather in China

Amid widespread condemnation of the proposal, Pauline Hanson also wants to scrap existing parent and aged parent visa program

One Nation has vowed to cut Australia’s refugee intake by 90% and scrap the permanent parent visa program under its latest hardline plan to slash migration.

Pauline Hanson announced the policy on Tuesday, labelling it a “tough” approach to migration. It was quickly criticised by political opponents and advocacy groups who labelled the announcement a “predictable and cheap” attack on refugees.

items.title: European Commission accused of sugarcoating figures to release funds to Egypt
items.summary:
Leaked documents raise questions about claims Egypt met welfare targets to qualify for €2.5bn in loans

The European Commission has been accused of sugarcoating figures to enable it to release funds to Egypt under a landmark pact with the authoritarian government of Abdel Fatah al-Sisi.

The charge relates to a €7.4bn deal promised by Ursula von der Leyen, the European Commission president, to al-Sisi on a high-profile visit to Cairo in 2024. The three-year “strategic and comprehensive partnership” was intended to bolster Egypt’s shaky economy, deter migrants from coming to Europe and shore up a region reeling from the 7 October attacks and Israel’s war on Gaza.

Wage rates climb about 1 percentage point faster than before pandemic, triggering warnings of a sixth RBA rate rise

Wages grew at their fastest pace since late 2023 over the three months to September, buoyed up by this year’s boost to minimum pay rates for millions of lower paid workers – but still not fast enough to keep up with the rising cost of living.

The Australian Bureau of Statistics’ wage price index climbed by 1.1% in the most recent quarter, lifting the annual increase to 3.5% – a pace that economists said would keep the Reserve Bank on edge about the need for further interest rate hikes.

Law reform body recommends ongoing ban on commercial surrogacy, but greater compensation for surrogates, and safeguards around who the child’s legal parents are

Surrogates would be entitled to full compensation, with a nationally consistent framework ensuring domestic surrogacy is a viable option to parenthood, under proposed changes by Australia’s law reform body.

The Australian Law Reform Commission has been investigating how to better regulate surrogacy and harmonise laws so they are consistent with international legal obligations, while protecting human rights – particularly the rights and best interests of the child.

Gamers across Australia are preparing for the once-in-a-generation release of Grand Theft Auto VI, a day acolytes of the franchise say will be bigger than the biggest sporting events.

items.title: Sleeve checks and no smartglasses: South Korea races to protect all-important university exams against AI
items.summary:
South Korea has been gripped by revelations of AI-aided cheating, just days before more than half a million students are to sit high-stakes entrance exams

The integrity of South Korea’s career-defining university entrance exam has been thrown into doubt after the top scorer in a recent professional exam admitted using a concealed camera and AI to cheat.

On Thursday, more than half a million people, mostly school students, are due to sit the exam, known as the suneung, at 1,312 centres across the country. The exam runs for a gruelling eight hours over a single day and determines which university a candidate can attend and, in turn, their future prospects.

An eight-year-old Haitian boy who was put into restraints and detained by immigration agents in San Diego on 4 November and transferred to a facility in Texas has been reunited with his family in California.

Representative Juan Vargas shared a photograph of the boy and his family in a social media post on Monda, writing: “11 days ago, an 8-year-old in San Diego was taken into federal custody during an immigration check-in. items.title: How Ukraine struck the Kerch bridge, a symbol of Putin’s rule
items.summary:
With the SpaceX satellite system faltering, Ukraine’s military launched a surprise, multi-pronged attack to take down vital bridge to Crimea

At 10pm on Monday evening a Ukrainian soldier scrawled a message on a kamikaze drone. It said simply: “The bridge is fucked.” He then added: “We will stand and Moscow will fall.” It was a freezing night, with a bright starry sky and no clouds. Lines of ice had formed on the drone’s bulky wings. Soon, it would be hurtling towards its target – about 500km to the south.

Typically the soldiers who gathered in this muddy field in central Ukraine were attacking oil refineries deep inside Russia. In recent months the work had become almost mundane: they had hit so many of them. The objective that evening, however, was unique. It was a structure personally associated with Vladimir Putin and his grandiose imperial ambitions.

Continue reading...
items.t: How Ukraine struck the Kerch bridge, a symbol of Putin’s rule

Alice and Ellen Kessler, the identical pop-singing twins who chose to jointly end their lives through assisted dying last year, said they had “reached rock bottom” due to health problems and had been relieved to be able to die together.

The demolition is not quite total, because the rail bridge is still standing, one line in operation – but the attack is an obvious embarrassment to Russia two days before Vladimir Putin is due to meet Donald Trump and Xi Jinping in Shenzhen.

In a Shenzhen square on a balmy evening, locals and tourists watched the dozens of glinting towers that make up the city’s skyline ripple through the colour spectrum – cyan and violet, cyber green, China’s national scarlet and gold – repeatedly flashing the words “Apec 2026”.

The Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit is a dream showcase for one of China’s most advanced cities, and the country’s leader, Xi Jinping, is basking in its neon glow.

Hundreds of people have been arrested in heated demonstrations against Donald Trump in Manila, as the US president arrived in the city for a leaders’ summit.

Organisers claimed as many as 10,000 people would be joining protests against Trump in the capital of the Philippines on Tuesday, where he is attending the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (Asean) summit. The crowds were expected to try to march to the summit site.

items.title: European-made pesticides named in 1,605 poisoning reports in Brazil last year
items.summary:
About a third of cases involved chemicals banned for use on EU farms, according to investigation by Unearthed and Public Eye

Pesticides sold by European chemical companies were named in more than 1,600 poisoning reports in Brazil last year, an investigation has found.

About a third of the cases involved chemicals banned from use on farms in the EU because of the risks they pose to people and the environment. But European companies are not banned from manufacturing these chemicals, as long as they export them overseas to countries where they are legally allowed to be used.

items.t: European-made pesticides named in 1,605 poisoning reports in Brazil last year

items.title: Five EU states announce plans for immigration ‘return hubs’ in Rwanda
items.summary:
Germany, Austria, Netherlands, Denmark and Greece likely to face challenges to policy criticised as ‘grave moral failing’

Five EU member states have announced plans to set up an offshore centre in Rwanda for people with no legal right to stay in Europe, in a pilot scheme that is expected to face legal challenges and has been denounced as “a grave moral failing”.

The five countries – Germany, Austria, the Netherlands, Denmark and Greece – are the first to seek to use the EU’s newly agreed returns law that allows people who have exhausted all avenues of appeal against their removal from Europe to be sent to a third country.

items.t: Five EU states announce plans for immigration ‘return hubs’ in Rwanda

An American basketball player has been arrested in Nigeria for allegedly attempting to smuggle 33.95kg (75lb) of marijuana into the country.

Nigeria’s National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA) said a 28-year-old player named as Greene Da’monte Khiree from the state of Georgia was arrested at Lagos’s main airport last Wednesday after he arrived on a flight from Thailand via the United Arab Emirates.

items.title: Relocation of Cape Town baboons to sanctuary ignites heated protests
items.summary:
Demonstrators tried to block vehicle carrying the baboons, whose capture authorities say is needed to protect both primate and human

The relocation of a troop of baboons in Cape Town to a wildlife sanctuary has triggered furious protests by local people opposed to their capture, which officials argue is necessary to stop human-wildlife conflict in the city.

The 44-member Waterfall troop (named after the area they mainly inhabit) was captured in the southern seaside suburb of Simon’s Town on Friday and Saturday. A second, smaller Seaforth troop is also due to be moved.
